rule: บุญ's senses split by what carries the merit. 3 is merit as a QUALITY — goodness held by a person or attaching to a relation — so นักบุญ, บุญคุณ and บุญธรรม file there. 2 is merit as a DEED performed, so every verb of merit-making and the occasions built round it file there. 4 is merit as a STOCK carried over from a former life, so anything about fortune arriving, running out, or having been earned together before files there, and that is where the death euphemisms sit. 1 (happiness) and 5 (helping others, which the RID scopes to ใจบุญ alone) take nothing on this list.

notes.h3: บุญ — the senses split by what CARRIES the merit
notes.text:
Every one of the thirteen is a genuine compound — all thirteen etymologies read
`X + บุญ`. No false splits on this head.

notes.h2: 2026-09-23 — พัน, บัง, บุญ (28 filed, 5 false-split, 1 spelling-variant, 3 left unfiled on purpose)
notes.h3: บุญ — the senses split by what CARRIES the merit
notes.text:
**Sense 4 is the one that earns its keep.** คู่บุญ says *ชาติก่อน* in its own
gloss; หมดบุญ and สิ้นบุญ both mean death by way of *อำนาจวาสนา* running out;
เดชะบุญ is luck arriving by the force of merit already banked. Four words, one
idea: merit as a balance you arrive holding.

notes.h2: 2026-09-23 — พัน, บัง, บุญ (28 filed, 5 false-split, 1 spelling-variant, 3 left unfiled on purpose)
notes.h3: บุญ — the senses split by what CARRIES the merit
notes.text:
* **บุญธรรม → 3, not 2.** Adoption is a meritorious act, which argues for 2. I
  put it in 3 because the บุญ here is not a deed performed but a quality standing
  in for blood — พ่อบุญธรรม is a father by virtue rather than by birth. Arguable.
* **อุ้มบุญ → 2.** Sense 2's gloss says *ตามหลักคำสอน*, according to the
  teaching, and surrogacy is a modern coinage no teaching addresses. I filed it
  as a deed anyway because that is what the word names. Sense 5 (ช่วยเหลือ
  เกื้อกูลผู้อื่น) fits the meaning better but the RID scopes sense 5 to ใจบุญ by
  name, and filing against an explicit scope note is worse than filing against a
  loose one.
